flags: Sezzle submitted applications to the OCC to charter a de novo national bank, Sezzle Bank, N.A., and to the FDIC for deposit insurance, and expects to apply to the Federal Reserve to become a bank holding company.

Sezzle and WebBank entered into Second Amended Bank Program Agreements expanding their program to SezzleCash and Sezzle Send (with a $30.0 million initial loan-retention threshold, expandable to $150.0 million) and increasing Sezzle's minimum tangible net worth covenant from $12.0 million to $100.0 million.

Sezzle raised its FY2026 guidance to approximately 42.5% Total Revenue growth, $190.0 million of Adjusted Net Income (48.8% YoY growth), and $5.45–$5.50 of Adjusted Net Income per Diluted Share, and introduced preliminary FY2027 guidance of $7.20 Adjusted Net Income per Diluted Share.

business_model.basis: Stated directly in the Business and MD&A sections of the FY2025 Form 10-K.
business_model.claim: Sezzle operates a digital shopping and payments platform primarily in the United States and Canada while winding down and exiting operations in India and certain European countries.
quotes: We operate in the United States and Canada, and are currently winding down and exiting operations in India and certain countries in Europe.

business_model.basis: Stated directly in Item 1 Business of the FY2025 Form 10-K based on internal order data.
business_model.claim: Approximately 81% of Sezzle's consumers who placed orders during 2025 were Gen Z and Millennial consumers, who use credit cards less frequently than older generations or lack access to traditional credit.
quotes: We focus on a young consumer base that is tech-savvy; approximately 81% of our consumers who placed orders during the year ended December 31, 2025 were comprised of the Gen Z and Millennial generations (ages 18–48).

business_model.basis: Stated directly in the Products descriptions in Item 1 of the FY2025 Form 10-K.
business_model.claim: Sezzle provides consumers with point-of-sale short-term installment credit products—including pay-in-four, pay-in-two, a pay-in-five beta, and customized merchant installment terms—alongside an upfront pay-in-full checkout option.
quotes: The Sezzle Platform offers a payments solution for consumers that instantly extends credit at the point-of-sale, allowing consumers to purchase and receive the ordered merchandise at the time of sale while paying in installments over time.

business_model.basis: Stated directly in Item 1 and Item 7 of the FY2025 Form 10-K.
business_model.claim: Sezzle offers optional recurring-fee subscriptions (Sezzle Premium and Sezzle Anywhere) and per-order Sezzle On-Demand financing using the Sezzle Virtual Card at non-integrated merchants, and refers consumers to third-party lenders for monthly fixed-rate installment loans up to $15,000.
quotes: Sezzle Anywhere is a paid subscription service that allows consumers to use their Sezzle Virtual Card at any merchant online or in-store, subject to certain merchant, product, goods, and service restrictions, for a recurring fee.

Through collaboration with third-party lenders, we enable our consumers at participating merchants access to interest-bearing monthly fixed-rate installment-loan products for larger-ticket items (up to $15,000), which extend up to 60 months.

business_model.basis: Stated directly in Item 1 of the FY2025 Form 10-K and Part I Item 2 of the Q3 2026 Form 10-Q.
business_model.claim: Sezzle expanded its consumer product suite with the stored-value wallet Sezzle Balance in 2025 and launched Sezzle Mobile, SezzleCash, and Sezzle Send in 2026.
quotes: In 2025, we launched a stored-value product that allows consumers to maintain funds within their Sezzle account for use toward eligible purchases or make payments on the Sezzle Platform (“Sezzle Balance”).
In 2026, we launched Sezzle Mobile, SezzleCash, and Sezzle Send.

business_model.basis: Stated directly in Item 1 and Item 7 of the FY2025 Form 10-K.
business_model.claim: Sezzle serves SMB and enterprise merchants across numerous verticals by paying merchants upfront net of a merchant processing fee while assuming consumer payment processing, fraud, and payment default costs and offering marketing and Sezzle Capital tools.
quotes: Our directly-integrated merchant segments are small-to-medium–sized businesses (“SMB”) and enterprise merchants, each spanning numerous verticals.

We generally pay our merchants the full transaction value upfront, net of the merchant processing fee owed to us, and assume all costs associated with consumer payment processing, fraud, and payment default.

business_model.basis: Stated directly in Item 1 of the FY2025 Form 10-K and Item 1.01 of the August 2026 Form 8-K.
business_model.claim: A substantial majority of short-term credit products on the Sezzle Platform are originated by WebBank, which retains SezzleCash and Sezzle Send loans on its balance sheet up to an initial $30.0 million threshold while Sezzle services all Program loans.
quotes: A substantial majority of the short-term credit products available on the Sezzle Platform are originated by our originating bank partner, WebBank, a Federal Deposit Insurance Company (“FDIC”)-insured Utah state-chartered industrial bank (“WebBank”).

WebBank will originate and fund the loans for both products and, in contrast to the sale structure applicable to the Company’s existing products, will retain those loans on its balance sheet to maturity, up to an aggregate retention threshold initially set at $30.0 million, and certain other exceptions.

business_model.basis: Stated directly in the Results of Operations table in Item 7 of the FY2025 Form 10-K.
business_model.claim: In 2025, Sezzle reported total revenue of $450,279 (table in thousands) across three categories: transaction income of $234,117 (table in thousands), income from other sources of 116,762 (table in thousands), and subscription revenue of 99,400 (table in thousands).
quotes: Our total revenue is classified into three categories: transaction income, subscription revenue, and income from other sources.

business_model.basis: Stated directly in Components of Results of Operations in Item 7 of the FY2025 Form 10-K and Item 2 of the Q3 2026 Form 10-Q.
business_model.claim: Transaction income comprises merchant processing fees (predominantly a percentage of volume plus a fixed per-transaction fee), partner interchange and promotional incentives, and consumer fees for card payments, failed payments, and Sezzle On-Demand finance charges.
quotes: Transaction income is comprised of all income earned from merchants, consumers, and other third parties that relate to placing and processing orders on the Sezzle Platform.

Such fees are assessed when consumers makes a scheduled payment using a card, when a payment method fails when attempting to make an installment payment, or when consumers pay a finance charge to use Sezzle On-Demand.

business_model.basis: Stated directly in Item 1A and Item 7 of the FY2025 Form 10-K and Item 2 of the Q3 2026 Form 10-Q.
business_model.claim: Paid subscriptions accounted for 22% of Sezzle's 2025 revenue, with subscription revenue driven by growth in Active Subscribers—reaching 955 in the third quarter of 2026 (table in thousands)—alongside pricing and subscriber retention.
quotes: For the year ended December 31, 2025, we derived 22% of our revenue from paid subscriptions and we expect subscription revenue to represent a key component of our total revenue in the future.
The increase in subscription revenue was primarily driven by the overall growth in our Active Subscribers.
The increase in Active Consumers and Active Subscribers is attributed to increased marketing and advertising initiatives, as well as new product releases.

business_model.basis: Stated directly in Results of Operations in Item 7 of the FY2025 Form 10-K.
business_model.claim: Income from other sources consists of late payment fees, gateway fees, and affiliate marketing revenue, with consumer late payment fees increasing to $74.0 million in 2025 from $25.2 million in 2024 due to fee standardization and higher past-due order volumes.
quotes: Consumer late payment fees totaled $74.0 million and $25.2 million for the years ended December 31, 2025 and 2024, respectively.
The increase in late payment fees was primarily driven by the standardizing of late payment fees along with a higher number of orders becoming past due as a result of GMV growth.

business_model.basis: Stated directly in Item 1A and Item 7 of the FY2025 Form 10-K and Item 2 of the Q3 2026 Form 10-Q.
business_model.claim: Total revenue is driven by platform transaction volume—measured starting in the third quarter of 2026 as TTV, which reached $1,398,249 (table in thousands) in that quarter—alongside active consumer engagement, new product adoption, and fourth-quarter holiday seasonality.
quotes: The increase in TTV was driven by increased usage of our Sezzle Anywhere and Sezzle Premium subscription products, as well as the launch of SezzleCash.
Total revenue and TTV in the fourth quarter have historically been strongest for us, in line with consumers generally spending more during the holiday shopping season.

business_model.basis: Stated directly in the Consolidated Statements of Operations in the Q3 2026 Form 10-Q and Form 8-K earnings release.
business_model.claim: For the first nine months of 2026, total revenue reached $451,725 (table in thousands) compared with $320,410 (table in thousands) in the prior-year period.

business_model.basis: Stated directly in the Q3 2026 income statement and Item 7 of the FY2025 Form 10-K.
business_model.claim: The provision for credit losses—81,949 in the first nine months of 2026 (table in thousands) and $89,298 in 2025 (table in thousands)—is a major operating expense driven by transaction volume, underwriting adjustments, holiday seasonality, and macroeconomic conditions.
quotes: The provision for credit losses is a significant component of our operating expenses, and excessive exposure to consumer repayment failure may impact our results of operations.
Of the $34.3 million increase when comparing the years ended December 31, 2025 and 2024, approximately $30.3 million was attributable to the increase in GMV.

business_model.basis: Stated directly in the Q3 2026 income statement and Item 7 of the FY2025 Form 10-K.
business_model.claim: Transaction expense—57,600 in the first nine months of 2026 (table in thousands) and $65,961 in 2025 (table in thousands)—consists primarily of third-party payment processing fees moved by transaction volume and processing efficiency, plus affiliate fees and consumer communications.
quotes: Transaction expense primarily comprises processing fees paid to third parties to process debit, credit and ACH payments received from consumers, merchant affiliate program and partnership fees, and consumer communication costs.
GMV growth outpaced the increase in payment processing expenses as a result of more efficient processing strategies in place in the current year.

business_model.basis: Stated directly in the Q3 2026 income statement and Item 7 of the FY2025 Form 10-K.
business_model.claim: Remaining operating expenses in the first nine months of 2026 (table in thousands) comprised marketing, advertising, and tradeshows of 46,535, personnel of 46,196, third-party technology and data of 15,818, and general and administrative of 15,379, driven by consumer acquisition, platform scaling, and strategic projects.
quotes: The increase in marketing, advertising, and tradeshow costs was from expanding initiatives to promote consumer acquisition and co-market the Sezzle brand.

The increase was primarily from higher professional service fees related to corporate strategic projects, consisting of costs related to the ongoing support for the antitrust litigation, our evaluation of a potential bank charter, and general capital markets exploration.

business_model.basis: Stated directly in the Q3 2026 balance sheet and income statement, Item 1A, and Item 7 of the FY2025 Form 10-K.
business_model.claim: Because Sezzle pays merchants upfront before collecting consumer installments, it funds receivables through a SOFR-based revolving line of credit (102,178 net in the 2026 third-quarter balance sheet, table in thousands) and a fixed-rate Delayed Settlement Incentive Program, driving net interest expense of (9,046) in the first nine months of 2026 (table in thousands).
quotes: Our business model involves paying merchants for goods upon a consumer’s purchase (less merchant processing fees) before we have received the full payment of the goods from a consumer utilizing the Sezzle Platform.

We incur interest expense on a continuous basis as a result of draws on our revolving line of credit to fund consumer notes receivable as well as our Delayed Settlement Incentive Program, whereby merchants may delay their payments owed by us in exchange for daily incentive payments.

business_model.basis: Stated directly in Item 1A of the FY2025 Form 10-K and Item 2 and Part II Item 1A of the Q3 2026 Form 10-Q.
business_model.claim: Competitive pressure for large merchants can compress merchant fees or require merchant incentives, while changing BNPL regulations and potential operation of Sezzle Bank, N.A. (applied for in October 2026) could increase compliance, operational, and capital costs.
quotes: Competition, particularly for large or high-volume merchants, may require us to reduce merchant fees, increase incentives or otherwise modify our pricing.

Establishing and operating the Bank will require us to contribute significant capital to the Bank and is likely to result in other new costs, which may be significant and could reduce or offset some or all of the anticipated benefits of the bank charter.

competitive_position.basis: stated in the cited item (10-K Item 1A Risk Factors)
competitive_position.claim: Sezzle faces intense competition in an industry with low barriers to entry against substantially larger banks, card networks, technology firms, and fintech lenders.
quotes: We operate in a highly competitive and dynamic industry with a low barrier to entry, which makes increased competition more likely.
Some of our competitors are substantially larger and have greater financial, technological, operational and marketing resources than we do.

competitive_position.basis: stated in the cited item (10-K Item 1A Risk Factors)
competitive_position.claim: Competition for large or high-volume merchants pressures Sezzle to cut merchant fees or offer upfront cash payments, rebates, and marketing incentives under multi-year contracts.
quotes: Competition, particularly for large or high-volume merchants, may require us to reduce merchant fees, increase incentives or otherwise modify our pricing.

These merchant partnership cost structures may not be cost-effective for us and we cannot assure you that the revenue we generate from the merchants we acquire will ultimately exceed the cost of adding them to our platform.

competitive_position.basis: stated in the cited items (10-K Item 1A and Item 7)
competitive_position.claim: Competitors could replicate or undercut Sezzle's paid subscription benefits, while costly consumer acquisition and high turnover could raise overhead expenses.
quotes: In addition, we operate in a highly competitive environment in which competitors may introduce similar subscription products at lower prices, bundle comparable benefits with other services, or offer more extensive or differentiated benefits that consumers find more attractive.
The acquisition of new consumers is costly and high turnover in our consumer base could result in higher than anticipated overhead costs.

competitive_position.basis: stated in the cited items (10-Q income statement, 10-K Item 1A, and 10-K Item 7)
competitive_position.claim: Because Sezzle's loans are unsecured and uncollateralized, weaker economic conditions or looser underwriting can raise credit losses, with provision for credit losses reaching 81,949 (table in thousands) in the first nine months of 2026.
quotes: Personal loans facilitated through our platform are not secured by any collateral, not guaranteed or insured by any third party, and not backed by any governmental authority in any way.
In weaker economic environments, consumers may have less disposable income to spend and so may be less likely to purchase merchandise by utilizing our services.

competitive_position.basis: stated in the cited items (10-K Item 1A and 10-Q balance sheet)
competitive_position.claim: Paying merchants upfront makes Sezzle reliant on its $225.0 million revolving credit facility, whose borrowing capacity fluctuates with pledged consumer notes receivable.
quotes: Our existing $225.0 million revolving credit facility is secured by our consumer notes receivable we choose to pledge and is subject to certain operating covenants.

Thus, a significant portion of our funding capacity is in part dependent on our accounts receivable, which can be volatile and, at times, at levels low enough to result in our inability to draw down on a portion of our credit facility.

competitive_position.basis: stated in the cited items (10-K Item 1A and 10-Q Item 2)
competitive_position.claim: Increasing BNPL scrutiny by U.S. state regulators and attorneys general, alongside potential federal policy shifts, could raise compliance costs, restrict operations, or encourage new entrants via deregulation.
quotes: The BNPL industry has become subject to increased regulatory scrutiny, and our failure to manage our business to comply with new regulations would materially and adversely affect our business, results of operations and financial condition.
In addition, deregulation of our industry, including as a result of policies adopted by the new administration, may encourage additional market entrants.

competitive_position.basis: stated in the cited item (10-Q Part II Item 1A Risk Factors)
competitive_position.claim: Sezzle's 2026 applications for a de novo national bank charter and FDIC deposit insurance may be denied, delayed, or conditioned, and would add significant capital and compliance costs if approved.
quotes: On October 22, 2026, we submitted an application to the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (the “OCC”) to charter a de novo national bank, Sezzle Bank, N.A. (the “Bank”), and an application to the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation (the “FDIC”) for deposit insurance.

Our applications may be denied, regulatory approval may be delayed or subject to conditions that we are unable or unwilling to satisfy, and there may be changes in applicable laws, regulatory policy, or supervisory expectations, including as a result of changes in agency priorities, that affect the review of our applications or the Bank’s operations.

competitive_position.basis: stated in the cited item (10-K Item 1A Risk Factors)
competitive_position.claim: Viral social media complaints, boycotts, or negative publicity at partner merchants could rapidly damage Sezzle's brand and reduce platform usage.
quotes: The use of social media by us and our consumers accelerates and amplifies our reputational risks in ways we may not be able to directly control or effectively manage, including by giving users the ability to more effectively organize collective actions such as boycotts, coordinated complaint campaigns and other brand-damaging behaviors.

Moreover, because our brand is directly associated with the brands of so many other companies by virtue of our business model and the integration of our platform with those of our partner merchants, there is a risk that we could be adversely affected by negative publicity that our partner merchants experience which is beyond our control.
